newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee dives by 12 pct on spec sell-off.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee dives by 12 pct on spec sell-off.

text.p: LIFFE robusta coffee futures took a sharp tumble with benchmark July ending Monday midsession 12 percent down on speculative sell-off after New York's dive on Friday.
The market was called as much as $500 a tonne lower as arabica futures came under frantic speculative selling to end Friday some 12 percent lower.
London's July came in $270 down at $2,200 and sank further to an intraday low of $2,130 before standing at $2,170 by midsession, still a whopping $300 lower.
But traders said it was still to early to tell if the five-month rally in both London and New York was coming to an end.
"Although there was a tremendous punch in the stomach (on Friday) it was not a knock out yet," said one.

"The good news is...the uptrend line is still intact," he added. "I am still a buyer." In essence, this morning's buying support in London came from the trade as speculators were taking their profits.

Chartwise, July's ability to move back above the key chart gap -- as seen a breakway gap -- of between $2,140 and $2,102 based on the second continuation chart proved that the market was still on the uptrend.
It touched a low of $2,130 before moving up again. "A break below $2,140 would be a bit less comfortable," said one.
Second-month position September was also $300 down at $2,200 after a low of $2,150.
Volume reached 4,453 lots, against dominated by the two front months contracts.
Based on London's performance, New York is now called to open $4 higher. New York's July plunged by 38.40 cents, the biggest single-day loss, to end Friday at 276.40.
Broker GNI said Friday's losses might continue for a while as there was no immediate signs of crop-damaging cold in Brazil.

Brazil is at the start of the frost season. There was no frost over the weekend and no damaging cold was forceast for the coffee areas for this weekend. -- Jalil Hamid, London newsroom +44 171 542 4985
